title: Round 3 — Provence, the Pitch & the Silver Screen

questions.question: What is the name of the strong, cold, dry wind that funnels down the Rhône valley to the Mediterranean coast of Provence?
questions.note: The Mistral is a cold, dry north-westerly wind funnelled down the Rhône valley toward the Gulf of Lion.

questions.question: In what year did England and France meet in football for the very first time, a match England won 4–1 in Paris?
questions.note: England dominated the early years, winning 10 of the first 11 meetings before France grew into a football superpower.

questions.question: Socca, a thin pancake made from chickpea flour and baked in a wood-fired oven, is a famous street-food speciality of which French Riviera city?
questions.note: Socca is a chickpea-flour pancake most closely associated with the old town of Nice.

questions.question: Who directed the 1993 science-fiction film Jurassic Park?
questions.note: Spielberg directed the original Jurassic Park, adapted from Michael Crichton's 1990 novel.

questions.question: A 'connoisseur' is an expert judge of taste. The word comes from an Old French verb meaning what?
questions.note: English froze the 18th-century French spelling 'connoisseur' even after French itself reformed it to 'connaisseur'.

questions.question: The famous seafront promenade in Nice, the 'Promenade des Anglais', takes its name from wealthy winter visitors of which nationality?
questions.note: The name literally means 'Walkway of the English', after the British who wintered in Nice and helped fund the path from 1820.

questions.question: The Gorges du Verdon, one of Europe's deepest canyons, reaches a maximum depth of roughly how many metres?
questions.note: The Verdon river has cut a limestone ravine up to about 700 metres deep between Castellane and Moustiers-Sainte-Marie.

questions.question: Which France player scored two goals in stoppage time to beat England 2–1 in their group match at Euro 2004?
questions.note: A free-kick and a penalty in added time snatched a win England had looked to have wrapped up.

questions.question: Pastis, the celebrated apéritif of Marseille, is flavoured mainly with which spice?
questions.note: Pastis is an anise-flavoured spirit traditionally served diluted with water, turning cloudy in the glass.

questions.question: Which British actor played park founder John Hammond in the 1993 film Jurassic Park?
questions.note: Attenborough, already an Oscar-winning director for Gandhi, took the Hammond role after a long acting hiatus.

questions.question: In 1309 the popes moved their residence from Rome to which city in the south of France, where seven popes then reigned until 1377?
questions.note: This period is known as the Avignon Papacy, and the popes' fortified Palais des Papes still dominates the city.

questions.question: Long before it meant an over-used phrase, a 'cliché' was originally what object in French printing?
questions.note: The word is onomatopoeic, imitating the 'click' of the die striking molten metal to cast a reusable plate.

questions.question: The Camargue wetlands are famous for their wild white horses, sea salt, and which pink wading birds?
questions.note: The Camargue's saline lagoons are one of Europe's few nesting sites for the greater flamingo.

questions.question: In French, 'un smoking' is a formal garment worn in the evening. What is it called in English?
questions.note: The French borrowed it from the Victorian 'smoking jacket', an indoor coat that evolved into formal evening wear.

questions.question: In which year did the Stade de France, the French national stadium in Saint-Denis, open its doors?
questions.note: It was inaugurated on 28 January 1998 with a France–Spain friendly, months before France won the World Cup there.

questions.question: Provence is the world's leading producer of which colour of wine?
questions.note: The vast majority of Provence's wine output is rosé, making it the global leader in premium rosé.

questions.question: Which British monarch regularly wintered on the French Riviera at Cimiez in Nice, where the Excelsior Regina Palace was built in 1897 to accommodate her?
questions.note: Queen Victoria's stays made Nice a fashionable royal destination, and a marble statue of her still stands at Cimiez.

questions.question: The 2011 French film 'The Artist' won which top Academy Award, becoming the first mostly silent feature to do so since 1929?
questions.note: 'The Artist', by Michel Hazanavicius, won five Oscars including Best Picture and Best Actor for Jean Dujardin.

questions.question: The Pont Saint-Bénézet, the medieval 'Pont d'Avignon' of the famous song, was originally built with 22 arches. How many still stand today?
questions.note: Repeated Rhône floods destroyed most of the bridge, leaving just four of its original 22 arches.

questions.question: Bryan Robson scored against France at the start of England's 1982 World Cup opener after how many seconds — then a World Cup record?
questions.note: England went on to win 3–1 in Bilbao, and Robson's record stood for 20 years.

questions.question: The Provençal spread tapenade takes its name from 'tapenas', the local word for which ingredient?
questions.note: Though olives dominate the paste, tapenade is named after the Provençal word for capers.

questions.question: Who directed the 2015 film Jurassic World, the reboot set on Isla Nublar?
questions.note: Trevorrow directed Jurassic World (2015), the fourth film in the franchise.

questions.question: The Roman aqueduct bridge known as the Pont du Gard was built to carry water to which Provençal city, the Roman Nemausus?
questions.note: The three-tiered bridge, nearly 49 metres high, crossed the river Gardon as part of a 50-kilometre aqueduct supplying Nîmes.

questions.question: In France, when someone says they are going to 'faire du footing', what activity are they doing?
questions.note: 'Footing' is a French pseudo-anglicism for jogging; in English 'footing' actually means balance or a foothold.

questions.question: The Calanques — a national park of narrow white limestone inlets on the Mediterranean — line the coast between Marseille and which small Provençal port town?
questions.note: The Parc National des Calanques stretches for about 20 km of limestone coast between Marseille and Cassis.

questions.question: Which England forward scored both goals in the 2–0 win over France at Wembley in the 1966 World Cup group stage?
questions.note: The victory sent hosts England through and knocked France out on their run to lifting the trophy.

questions.question: The calisson, a diamond-shaped sweet from Aix-en-Provence, is made from ground almonds and which candied fruit?
questions.note: Candied melon makes up the bulk of the candied fruit in a genuine calisson d'Aix.

questions.question: Released in 1962 and starring Sean Connery, what was the title of the first James Bond film?
questions.note: 'Dr. No', directed by Terence Young from Ian Fleming's novel, launched the long-running British Bond series.

questions.question: French children play 'le baby-foot'. What is this game called in English?
questions.note: A pseudo-anglicism from 'baby' plus 'foot' (football); its name is credited to French inventor Lucien Rosengart in the 1930s.

questions.question: Which British statesman and former Lord Chancellor popularised Cannes as a resort after settling there in 1834 and building the Villa Éléonore-Louise?
questions.note: Brougham's enthusiasm for the town's mild winters drew British and European aristocracy and helped turn a fishing village into a glamorous resort.
